tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge a Single Misdemeanor Conviction as a First Offender (R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-1.3-2)

controllingAuthority.summary: A first offender — a person convicted of a felony or misdemeanor who has not previously been convicted of or placed on probation for a felony or misdemeanor, and who has no pending criminal proceeding — may move to expunge a misdemeanor conviction five years after completion of sentence, where the person has not been convicted of a crime of violence, has no pending criminal proceeding, has had no felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction during the lookback period, and has paid or obtained waiver or reduction of all court-imposed or court-related financial obligations. Relief is discretionary on findings of good moral character, rehabilitation to the court's satisfaction, and consistency with the public interest.

exclusions: Any conviction for a crime of violence as statutorily defined: murder, manslaughter, first-degree arson, kidnapping with intent to extort, robbery, larceny from the person, first- and second-degree sexual assault, first- and second-degree child molestation, assault with intent to murder, assault with intent to rob, assault with intent to commit first-degree sexual assault, burglary, and entering a dwelling with intent to commit murder, robbery, sexual assault or larceny.
Any person previously convicted of, or placed on probation for, a felony or misdemeanor; prior probation alone defeats first-offender status.
Any felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction during the five-year lookback. An arrest alone, without conviction, defeats eligibility.
Any pending criminal proceeding.
Court-imposed or court-related financial obligations that are unpaid and not waived or reduced by court order.
Federal, out-of-state, military and tribal records.

waitingPeriods.duration: 5 years from completion of sentence, including completion of probation

waitingPeriods.condition: Lookback free of any felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction

units.label: BCI record, docket and eligibility classification
units.description: The judgment stage. Pull the BCI criminal history and the court docket, obtain the BCI number the forms require, and classify the case: first-offender status including prior probation, the crime-of-violence bar, whether the sentence and any probation are complete, whether any arrest or conviction fell inside the lookback, whether financial obligations are paid, waived or reduced, and whether the offence has been reclassified by the General Assembly so the reclassification overlay applies. Nothing is filed at this stage and LegalEase never receives, inspects or authenticates any record.

units.label: Court-specific Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit, with the proposed order
units.description: The document stage. The correct court's Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit is completed — District Court form DC-33, the Superior Court misdemeanor version, or the Family Court misdemeanor form, according to where the conviction occurred. The form requires the defendant's name, case number, BCI number, counts, charges, dispositions and the charging police department, and requires the filer to elect seal or expunge — a legal choice with different consequences, never a checkbox preference. The proposed order is prepared to be brought to the hearing for the judge's signature. A custom pleading is not advisable: the Judiciary publishes the forms and the affidavit must be sworn.

units.label: Notice to the Attorney General and charging police department, the hearing, and delivery of certified orders
units.description: The procedural stage, which runs after the packet exists and continues after the judge signs. File with the clerk, who fills in the hearing date; the hearing must be at least ten days after filing because notice must reach the Attorney General and the charging police department. Sign the affidavit before a notary or clerk. Attend the hearing with the proposed order. On a grant the clerk prepares three certified copies after all conditions are satisfied, and the petitioner delivers one to the Attorney General's BCI unit and one to the charging police department — if that delivery does not happen, nothing changes on the record. Verify afterwards with a fresh BCI record.

rules.filing: File the correct court's Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit, with the proposed order, with the clerk of the court where the conviction occurred. The clerk fills in the hearing date.
rules.fees: No expungement filing fee in the Superior Court. The Rhode Island Superior Court's own expungement FAQ, 'Is there a fee associated with my expungement?' (https://www.courts.ri.gov/Courts/superiorcourt/Pages/FAQs.aspx), expressly says the process requires no fee; R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-1.3-3 (https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE12/12-1.3/12-1.3-3.htm) is the statutory branch for the route's own conditions. Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research handoff. This is court-specific, not a national fee rule: fines, costs, restitution and other obligations already ordered in the underlying case remain the participant's and remain the separate statutory eligibility condition; a no-fee filing cancels no unpaid court obligation, and no filing-fee-waiver application is required solely to waive a $0 filing fee. No dollar amount is attributed to Superior-55 or any form without locating it in that form's own text.
rules.feeWaiver: Not stated for the motion itself. Court-imposed financial obligations on the underlying case may be waived or reduced by court order, and that waiver or reduction satisfies the eligibility condition.
rules.notice: Notice must be given to the Rhode Island Department of Attorney General and to the police department that brought the charge, at least ten days before the hearing. A hearing is required. The court may grant if it finds no felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction during the lookback, no pending criminal proceeding, financial obligations satisfied or waived or reduced, good moral character, rehabilitation to the court's satisfaction, and that expungement is consistent with the public interest.
rules.service: Serve the Attorney General and the charging police department at least ten days before the hearing. After a grant, the petitioner delivers certified copies of the order to the Attorney General's BCI unit and the charging police department.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the affidavit before a notary or a clerk. This is a sworn document and the signature must be witnessed in person.
rules.notarization: Required. The affidavit must be signed before a notary or a clerk.

researchParticipantText.fee: The Rhode Island Superior Court does not charge an expungement filing fee. This is separate from fines, costs, restitution, or other obligations already ordered in your case. Follow the requirements for your particular expungement route concerning any remaining obligations. A no-fee filing does not cancel an unpaid court obligation.

selfHelpStopConditions: Any crime of violence, which bars conviction expungement outright.
Any prior conviction or prior probation, which defeats first-offender status.
Any arrest during the lookback period, even without a conviction.
Unpaid or unclear court financial obligations.
Any pending criminal proceeding.
The good moral character and rehabilitation showing, which is the court's finding and not a fact LegalEase can supply.
Immigration exposure. Rhode Island expungement does not resolve immigration consequences.

Any goal involving law enforcement employment, bar admission or bar character and fitness, a teaching certificate, a coaching certificate, or early childhood education work, where disclosure survives expungement.
Federal, out-of-state, military and tribal records, which Rhode Island relief does not reach.

units.label: BCI record, docket and eligibility classification
units.description: The judgment stage. Pull the BCI criminal history and the court docket, obtain the BCI number the forms require, and classify the case: first-offender status including prior probation, the crime-of-violence bar, whether the sentence and any probation are complete, whether any arrest or conviction fell inside the lookback, whether financial obligations are paid, waived or reduced, and whether the offence has been reclassified by the General Assembly so the reclassification overlay applies. Nothing is filed at this stage and LegalEase never receives, inspects or authenticates any record.

units.label: Court-specific Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit, with the proposed order
units.description: The document stage. The correct court's Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit is completed for each conviction being cleared. The form requires the defendant's name, case number, BCI number, counts, charges, dispositions and the charging police department, and requires the filer to elect seal or expunge — a legal choice with different consequences, never a checkbox preference. The proposed order is prepared to be brought to the hearing for the judge's signature. A custom pleading is not advisable: the Judiciary publishes the forms and the affidavit must be sworn.

units.label: Notice to the Attorney General and charging police department, the hearing, and delivery of certified orders
units.description: The procedural stage, which runs after the packet exists and continues after the judge signs. File with the clerk, who fills in the hearing date; the hearing must be at least ten days after filing because notice must reach the Attorney General and the charging police department. Sign the affidavit before a notary or clerk. Attend the hearing with the proposed order. On a grant the clerk prepares three certified copies after all conditions are satisfied, and the petitioner delivers one to the Attorney General's BCI unit and one to the charging police department — if that delivery does not happen, nothing changes on the record. Verify afterwards with a fresh BCI record.

Have you ever been convicted of a felony?

controllingAuthority.summary: Section 12-1.3-1(5) provides that 'misdemeanor' includes, but is not limited to, those crimes previously classified as felonies under law at the time the original sentence was imposed but reclassified by the general assembly as a misdemeanor in the interim, prior to the time the motion to expunge is brought. tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge Records of a Completed Deferred Sentence (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 12-19-19, 12-1.3-2(e))
tracks.publicName: Clear a record after completing a deferred sentence

controllingAuthority.summary: A person who received a deferred sentence may move for expungement after completion of the deferred sentence. If the court finds after a hearing that the person complied with all terms of the deferral agreement, including payment of fines, fees, costs, assessments and restitution, the person becomes immediately eligible for consideration for expungement. There is no waiting period beyond completion. The court must also find no pending criminal proceedings and good moral character, and no person convicted of a crime of violence may have deferred-sentence records expunged. A deferred sentence is not an automatic expungement: the court process and the hearing are still required.

exclusions: Any person convicted of a crime of violence, who may not have deferred-sentence records expunged.
Any deferral where the terms are not complete, including unpaid fines, fees, costs, assessments or restitution.
Any pending criminal proceeding.
Federal, out-of-state, military and tribal records.

units.description: The document stage. The correct court's Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit is completed, on the same form set as the general conviction tracks. The form requires the defendant's name, case number, BCI number, counts, charges, dispositions and the charging police department, and requires the filer to elect seal or expunge — a legal choice with different consequences, never a checkbox preference. The proposed order is prepared to be brought to the hearing for the judge's signature. A custom pleading is not advisable: the Judiciary publishes the forms and the affidavit must be sworn.

On a grant the clerk prepares three certified copies after all conditions are satisfied, and the petitioner delivers one to the Attorney General's BCI unit and one to the charging police department — if that delivery does not happen, nothing changes on the record. tracks.legalName: Automatic Expungement of Marijuana Possession Records (R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-1.3-5)
tracks.publicName: Check that an old marijuana possession record has been cleared

controllingAuthority.summary: A person with a prior civil violation, misdemeanor conviction or felony conviction for possession only of a marijuana offence since decriminalized is entitled to automatic expungement, notwithstanding the general Chapter 12-1.3 rules. Records were to be expunged before 1 July 2024 on a timeline set by the chief justice, with an expedited procedure available on written request. Where the amount is not stated in the record the court presumes two ounces or less. Pending cases, prior convictions and violent convictions do not block the relief; outstanding fines, fees and costs do not block it and eligible marijuana-related amounts are waived; other counts in the same case do not prevent expungement of the eligible marijuana count; and a marijuana expungement under this section is not treated as a prior conviction or civil adjudication for sentencing a later crime. Under subsection (e) anyone incarcerated for misdemeanor or felony marijuana possession has all court costs waived with respect to expungement. Under subsection (f) the court, not the participant, sends a copy of the order to the Attorney General, the arresting agency and any other agency known to hold records. Under subsection (m) custodians may not disclose the existence of the records on inquiry from any source, except from the individual, a bar admission or character and fitness or disciplinary body, the commissioner of elementary and secondary education, or a law enforcement agency where the nature of a new charge would be affected.

exclusions: Anything other than possession only. Possession with intent to distribute and distribution charges are not covered.
Marijuana offences that were not decriminalized under R.I. Gen. Laws § 21-28.11-22 thresholds.
Non-marijuana counts in the same case, which this section does not clear even though they do not block expungement of the eligible marijuana count.
Federal, out-of-state, military and tribal records.

Where the automatic action did not reach the record, the participant's signed expedited written request goes to the court in which the marijuana case was heard.

components.notes: The participant's expedited written request under § 12-1.3-5. Rhode Island publishes no official form, so it is drafted. Controlled contents only: the addressee and caption for the court in which the marijuana case was heard, the participant's identity, the case identifiers, a statement that the request is made under the § 12-1.3-5 expedited procedure, the participant-supplied qualifying facts (possession only, and the amount where the record states one), the relief requested, and a signature instruction. It does not certify that the automatic relief failed, decide disputed eligibility, invent supporting evidence, seek agency agreement, promise expedited treatment or argue the participant's case.

units.label: Verify the automatic § 12-1.3-5 expungement
units.description: The default stage, and the one that must run first. Section 12-1.3-5 entitles a person with a prior civil violation, misdemeanor conviction or felony conviction for possession only of a since-decriminalized marijuana offence to automatic expungement, and Rhode Island completed the initial statewide effort in June 2023 — more than 23,000 records, being 3,015 in Superior Court, 9,952 in the Traffic Tribunal and 10,650 in District Court — over a year ahead of the 1 July 2024 deadline. The participant pulls a BCI criminal history and checks whether the record has already cleared. Nothing is filed at this stage and no participant submission exists: the relief is automatic and, under § 12-1.3-5(f), the court rather than the participant distributes the order to the Attorney General, the arresting agency and any other agency known to hold records. Where the record has cleared, the route ends here and no motion is generated or sold.

units.label: Participant-signed expedited written request where the record has not cleared
units.description: The conditional stage, reached only where the participant confirms from their BCI record that the eligible marijuana possession record has not been expunged. Section 12-1.3-5 makes an expedited procedure available on written request, so the participant signs and submits a request to the court in which the marijuana case was heard. It seeks the same statutory legal effect as the automatic route — expungement of the same eligible marijuana count — so this is one mechanism with two stages, not two remedies. Rhode Island publishes no official form for the request, so it is drafted from controlled participant facts. The unit is unavailable until the verification stage establishes that the automatic action did not reach the record; it is never offered at the outset.
